title: Otto Loewi transferred a solution from one frog heart to another and showed that nerves release chemical substances

trailer.text: Otto Loewi, winner of the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, was born in Frankfurt, Germany, to a Jewish family of wine merchants.
At the beginning of the 20th century it was known that nerve signals are conveyed by electrical impulses, but it was unclear whether they are also conveyed by chemical substances.
According to his own account, the idea for the experiment came to him in a dream, and he got up, went to the laboratory and performed a simple experiment on a frog heart.
He transferred solution from a heart whose nerve had been stimulated to a second heart, and the second heart slowed as if its own nerve had been stimulated.
According to Loewi, this proved that nerves release chemical substances, and in 1936 he shared the Nobel Prize with Henry Dale.

stations.title: Before the experiment: an open question

paragraphs.text: Otto Loewi was born on June 3, 1873, in Frankfurt, the son of the Jewish wine merchant Jacob Loewi and Anna Willstätter.
According to the article, he received a classical education in Latin and Greek.
According to DGIM, the family that Loewi founded with his wife Guida and their four children acknowledged its Jewish identity but was not religious and was considered assimilated.
According to Loewi, he saw high mortality among tuberculosis and pneumonia patients left without treatment, and after this he decided to move to basic research.
He became a professor of pharmacology in Graz.
At the beginning of the 20th century it was known that the nervous system's signals are conveyed by electrical impulses.
It was unclear whether they are also conveyed by chemical substances.
According to Loewi himself, until 1921 it was not known how the stimulation of a nerve influences the effector organ.
The hypothesis of chemical transmission is usually credited to Elliott, who published it in 1904.
Loewi himself wrote that Elliott then suggested that the stimulation of sympathetic nerves might be brought about by the release of adrenaline.
In 1929 Fletcher recalled that Loewi had independently proposed the hypothesis as early as 1903, in a private conversation with him.
An earlier report by Dixon, in an obscure journal, hinted at an inhibitory substance released upon stimulation of the vagus nerve, but it received no attention.
According to an encyclopedia, by 1920 no decisive experimental evidence had yet been found, and the hypothesis had fallen into discredit among scientists.
According to the Medical University of Graz, Loewi was appointed in 1909 to the Chair of Pharmacology at the University of Graz, and taught there until 1938.

stations.title: A dream at night, a tiny slip of paper

paragraphs.text: According to his own account, the idea for the experiment came to him in a dream, at Easter.
Loewi recounted that on the night before Easter Sunday he awoke, turned on the light and jotted down a few notes on a tiny slip of paper.
In the morning he could not decipher his handwriting.
According to Dale, Loewi told him essentially the same story as early as 1921.
According to Dale, Loewi repeated it virtually unchanged over four decades.

Loewi recounted that the following night, at three in the morning, the idea came back to him, and he then got up immediately, went to the laboratory and performed a simple experiment on a frog heart according to the design that had come to him in the night.
According to his description, the hearts of two frogs were isolated: the first with its nerves, the second without.
According to his description, the vagus nerve of the first heart was stimulated for a few minutes, and the Ringer solution from that heart was transferred to the second heart.
The second heart slowed and its beats diminished, as if its own vagus nerve had been stimulated.
When the accelerator nerve was stimulated and the solution transferred, the second heart sped up and its beats increased.
According to Loewi, the results proved that the nerves do not influence the heart directly but release chemical substances.
According to the Nobel Prize website, the experiment in which he stimulated a frog heart with electrical impulses and transferred solution to another heart was performed in 1921.
The substance was called Vagusstoff.
The first paper began a series of fourteen papers on humoral transmission, published over the next fifteen years.
Only in the tenth and eleventh papers, in 1926, did Loewi and Navratil identify the Vagusstoff as acetylcholine.
Loewi showed that the action of the esterase could be inhibited by minute concentrations of eserine.
According to Loewi, after Dale and Dudley produced the substance directly from the organs, there could be no more doubt that the Vagusstoff is acetylcholine.
Only in 1936 did Loewi identify the substance released upon stimulation of the accelerator nerve as adrenaline.
Vagusstoff was the first confirmation of chemical synaptic transmission and the first neurotransmitter to be discovered.
The discovery led to a conceptual revolution in neurophysiology.
According to Loewi in his Nobel Lecture, a clear answer had at last been found to the age-old question of how the stimulus passes from nerve to organ.
According to Loewi, the proof that the nerve releases an inhibiting substance makes clear where peripheral inhibition comes from.
He called on clinicians in the future to consider these relationships in order to explain symptoms that until then had been regarded as purely reflex.
In 1926 Loewi was invited to demonstrate the experiment at the 12th International Congress of Physiology in Stockholm.
In 1936 he received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, jointly with Sir Henry Dale.
In his Nobel Lecture he thanked his collaborators Navratil, Witanowski and Engelhart.
In their acceptance speech, Dale and Loewi acknowledged Elliott and Dixon for their contributions.
In 1944 he received the Cameron Prize of the University of Edinburgh.
In 1954 he was appointed Foreign Member of the Royal Society.
The Research Center for Vascular Biology, Immunology and Inflammation at the Medical University of Graz bears his name.
The German neuroscience society (Neurowissenschaftliche Gesellschaft) has awarded the Otto Loewi Medal every four years since 2018.

stations.title: Arrest, exile and a lifelong friend

paragraphs.text: When the Germans invaded Austria in 1938, Loewi was forced to leave his homeland.
In March 1938 Loewi and two of his four children were imprisoned, like other male Jews in Graz.
According to the article, the Gestapo arrested him and his two sons at gunpoint, and he was released thanks to an international protest by scientists.
The Gestapo forced him to transfer his Nobel Prize money from a bank in Stockholm to a bank under Nazi control.
He was released two months later, and in September was allowed to leave for London.
On September 28, 1938, he fled to England and stayed with Henry Dale for a few weeks.
In 1902, in Starling's laboratory in London, Loewi first met Henry Dale, who became his lifelong friend and who later shared the Nobel Prize with him.
In 1940 he arrived in New York.
His wife Guida joined him in early 1941, having not been allowed to leave Austria before then.
On April 1, 1946, he was granted American citizenship.
Loewi died on Christmas Day 1961.
According to DGVS, he died in New York.
In a eulogy in 1962, Ferdinand Hoff said that an inhuman system had forced the great scholar into exile.
In accordance with his wishes, he was buried in August 1962 in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.
The first paper also raised another possibility: that the substances were a product of altered cardiac activity and not of the nerve stimulation itself.
It is said that Loewi failed more than once in his attempts to reproduce the experiment.
Some of the papers in the series were directed against the criticisms of Leon Asher.

The vagus nerve of the frog Loewi used contains inhibitory fibers and excitatory fibers, and in winter the inhibitory fibers are the majority, so Loewi was lucky to have carried out the experiments in February or March.
Under slightly different circumstances, the acetylcholine would have broken down before reaching the second heart.
According to Van der Kloot, the heart of the Hungarian frogs that Loewi used contains little cholinesterase.
Loewi doubted chemical transmission in voluntary motor nerves and in the central nervous system, because they act much more rapidly.
Dale and his associates were mainly responsible for proving that chemical transmission exists outside the postganglionic autonomic nervous system as well.

disagreements.question: In what year was the dream that preceded the experiment?

versions.says: According to DGIM, Loewi said the idea came to him in a dream at Easter 1921
In a quotation in an article in PubMed Central, the year given is 1920
According to another version in the encyclopedia, the dream was at Easter 1920
According to the Nobel Prize website, the experiment itself was performed in 1921

disagreements.question: When did Loewi arrive in New York?

versions.says: According to DGVS, on July 1, 1940, after sailing from Liverpool

disagreements.question: How old was Loewi when he died?

versions.says: According to the article in PubMed Central, 89

claims.text: אוטו לוי נולד ב-3 ביוני 1873 בפרנקפורט שבגרמניה, בן לסוחר יעקב לוי ולאנה וילשטטר.
claims.quote: Otto Loewi was born on June 3, 1873, in Frankfurt-am-Main, Germany, the son of Jacob Loewi, a merchant, and Anna Willstätter.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, לוי נולד בפרנקפורט למשפחה יהודית של סוחרי יין אמידים וקיבל חינוך קלאסי בלטינית וביוונית.
claims.quote: Born in Frankfurt, Germany, into a Jewish family of wealthy wine merchants, he received a classical education in Latin and Greek

claims.text: ב-1936 חלק לוי עם הנרי דייל את פרס נובל ברפואה או בפיזיולוגיה.
claims.quote: In 1936 Loewi shared with Henry Dale the Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for work relating to the chemical transmission of nervous impulses.

claims.text: בתחילת המאה ה-20 היה ידוע שאותות מערכת העצבים מועברים בעזרת אימפולסים חשמליים.
claims.quote: At the beginning of the 20th century, it was known that the nervous system’s signals are conveyed with the help of electrical impulses.

claims.text: לא היה ברור אם האותות מועברים גם בחומרים כימיים.
claims.quote: However, it was unclear whether the signals were also conveyed by chemical substances.

claims.text: לפי דבריו, הרעיון לניסוי עלה בחלום בפסחא 1921.
claims.quote: According to his own statements, the idea for the experiment had come to Loewi in a dream on Easter 1921

claims.text: לוי סיפר שקם מיד, הלך למעבדה וביצע ניסוי פשוט בלב צפרדע לפי התכנון הליליי.
claims.quote: I got up immediately, went to the laboratory, and performed a simple experiment on a frog heart according to the nocturnal design.

claims.text: לפי תיאורו, עצב הוואגוס של הלב הראשון גורה דקות אחדות, ותמיסת רינגר מהלב הועברה ללב השני.
claims.quote: The vagus nerve of the first heart was stimulated for a few minutes. Then the Ringer solution that had been in the first heart during the stimulation of the vagus was transferred to the second heart.

claims.text: הלב השני האט ופעימותיו נחלשו, כאילו עצב הוואגוס שלו גורה.
claims.quote: [This second heart] slowed and its beats diminished just as if its vagus had been stimulated.

claims.text: לפי לוי, התוצאות הוכיחו שהעצבים אינם משפיעים ישירות על הלב אלא משחררים חומרים כימיים.
claims.quote: These results unequivocally proved that the nerves do not influence the heart directly but liberate from their terminals specific chemical substances

claims.text: לפי המאמר, ב-1908 הפך לוי לפרופסור לפרמקולוגיה באוניברסיטת גראץ.
claims.quote: In 1908, Loewi became a professor of pharmacology at the University of Graz in Austria, gaining a reputation as a lively lecturer.

claims.text: לפי האוטוביוגרפיה, ב-1909 מונה לקתדרה לפרמקולוגיה בגראץ.
claims.quote: in 1909 he was appointed to the Chair of Pharmacology in Graz.

claims.text: לפי תיאורו, בודדו לבבות של שתי צפרדעים, הראשון עם עצביו והשני בלעדיהם.
claims.quote: The hearts of two frogs were isolated, the first with its nerves, the second without.

claims.text: לפי אתר פרס נובל, ב-1921 גירה לוי לב צפרדע באימפולסים חשמליים והעביר תמיסה ללב אחר.
claims.quote: In 1921 Otto Loewi stimulated the heart of a frog with electrical impulses and had it pump a small amount of nutrient solution.

claims.text: לוי קיבל את פרס נובל ב-1936 במשותף עם סר הנרי דייל.
claims.quote: It was for these researches that he received the Nobel Prize in 1936, jointly with Sir Henry Dale.

claims.text: לוי היה בנו של סוחר היין היהודי יעקב לוי ושל אשתו אנה.
claims.quote: Otto Loewi was the son of the Jewish wine merchant Jakob Loewi and his wife Anna, née Willstädter.

claims.quote: after seeing the high mortality in countless cases of far-advanced tuberculosis and pneumonia, left without any treatment because of lack of therapy

claims.text: לפי לוי עצמו, עד 1921 לא היה ידוע כיצד גירוי עצב משפיע על תפקוד האיבר המגיב.
claims.quote: Up until the year 1921 it was not known how the stimulation of a nerve influenced the effector organ’s function

claims.quote: Credit for the hypothesis is usually given to Elliott, who published the suggestion in 1904.

claims.quote: An earlier report by Walter Ernest Dixon, another English pharmacologist, had hinted at the possibility of the release of an inhibitory substance upon stimulation of the vagus nerve.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה, עד 1920 טרם נמצאה ראיה ניסויית מכרעת להעברה כימית, והשערה זו נפלה בדעת הקהל המדעי.
claims.quote: by 1920 no decisive experimental evidence for chemical transmission had yet been found, and the hypothesis had fallen into rather general discredit.

claims.text: לוי סיפר שבליל שלפני יום ראשון של הפסחא התעורר, הדליק אור ורשם כמה הערות על פתק זעיר.
claims.quote: The night before Easter Sunday of [1921] I awoke, turned on the light, and jotted down a few notes on a tiny slip of thin paper.

claims.text: לפי דייל, לוי סיפר לו בעצם את אותו סיפור ב-1921 וחזר עליו כמעט ללא שינוי במשך ארבעה עשורים.
claims.quote: Dale has testified that Loewi told him essentially the same story in 1921 and repeated it virtually unchanged several times during the next four decades.

claims.text: לפי המאמר, באחד הלבבות עצב הוואגוס היה שלם ובשני הוסר העצבוב.
claims.quote: one preparation had the vagus nerve intact, while the other was denervated. Next, he stimulated the vagus nerve supplying the first heart, causing it to beat more slowly

claims.text: כשגורה עצב המאיץ והתמיסה הועברה, הלב השני האיץ ופעימותיו התחזקו.
claims.quote: Similarly, when the accelerator nerve was stimulated and the Ringer from this period transferred, the second heart speeded up and its beats increased.

claims.quote: the first in a series of fourteen papers on humoral transmission which Loewi and his several collaborators published in the same journal during the next fifteen years.

claims.text: רק במאמרים העשירי והאחד-עשר ב-1926 זיהו לוי ונברטיל את ה-Vagusstoff כאצטילכולין.
claims.quote: But not until the tenth and eleventh papers (both published in 1926) did Loewi and his collaborator E. Navratil positively identify the Vagusstoff with acetylcholine.

claims.text: לוי הראה שניתן לעכב את פעולת האסטראז בריכוזים מזעריים של אזרין.
claims.quote: I was able to show furthermore that the action of this esterase could be specifically inhibited through minimum concentrations of eserine7.

claims.text: לפי לוי, לאחר שדייל ודודלי הפיקו את החומר ישירות מהאיברים, אין עוד ספק שה-Vagusstoff הוא אצטילכולין.
claims.quote: As Dale and Dudley9 were able to produce it directly from the organs, there can be no more doubt that the vagus substance is Ac.Ch.

claims.text: רק ב-1936 זיהה לוי באופן חיובי את החומר שמשתחרר בגירוי עצב המאיץ כאדרנלין.
claims.quote: it was not until 1936 that Loewi positively identified the Acceleransstoff or Sympathicusstoff with adrenaline (epinephrine)

claims.text: הגילוי הוביל למהפכה מושגית בנוירופיזיולוגיה.
claims.quote: This discovery in fact inaugurated a conceptual revolution in neurophysiology.

claims.text: לפי לוי בהרצאת הנובל, נמצאה סוף סוף תשובה ברורה לשאלה העתיקה על מהות העברת הגירוי מעצב לאיבר.
claims.quote: at last a clear answer has been found to the age-old question as to the nature of the stimulus-transfer from nerve to effector organ.

claims.text: לפי לוי, ההוכחה שהעצב משחרר חומר מעכב מבהירה את מקור העיכוב ההיקפי.
claims.quote: With the proof that this inhibition comes about because the nerve releases a function-inhibiting substance, the reason for it becomes clear.

claims.text: לוי קרא לרופאים בעתיד להתייחס ליחסים אלה כדי להסביר תסמינים שנחשבו עד כה רפלקסיביים בלבד.
claims.quote: It would be very desirable if in future clinicians would give consideration to these relationships

claims.quote: In their acceptance speech, they appropriately acknowledged the contributions of Elliott and Dixon.

claims.quote: and of the Cameron Prize of the University of Edinburgh (1944)

claims.quote: In Erinnerung an Otto Loewi trägt das Forschungszentrum für Gefäßbiologie, Immunologie und Entzündung an der Medizinischen Universität Graz seinen Namen.

claims.quote: The Neurowissenschaftliche Gesellschaft has been awarding the Otto Loewi Medal every four years to outstanding scientists in the field of neuroscience since 2018.

claims.quote: When the Germans invaded Austria in 1938, Loewi was forced to leave his homeland.

claims.quote: Like other male Jewish citizens of Graz, Loewi and two of his four children were imprisoned in March of that year.

claims.quote: In 1938, the Germans invaded Austria, and Loewi and his two sons were arrested by the Gestapo at gunpoint.

claims.text: אומרים שלוי נכשל לא פעם בניסיונותיו לשחזר את הניסוי.
claims.quote: it is said that he often failed in his own attempts to do so

claims.text: חלק מהמאמרים בסדרה כוונו נגד ביקורתו של ליאון אשר.
claims.quote: particularly Leon Asher, against whose criticisms some of the papers in the series were specifically directed.

claims.text: בנסיבות מעט שונות האצטילכולין היה מפורק לפני שהגיע ללב השני.
claims.quote: Under slightly different circumstances, acetylcholine would have been rapidly metabolised by cholinesterase before it could reach the second heart.

claims.text: לפי ואן דר קלוט, לב הצפרדעים ההונגריות שבהן השתמש לוי מכיל מעט כולינסטראז.
claims.quote: According to William Van der Kloot, the heart of the Hungarian frogs that Loewi used contains only a small amount of the cholinesterase

claims.text: לוי פקפק בהעברה כימית בעצבים מוטוריים רצוניים ובמערכת העצבים המרכזית, משום שהם פועלים מהר הרבה יותר.
claims.quote: Chiefly because nervous impulses produce their effects so much more rapidly in voluntary and central nervous processes than in autonomic, Loewi doubted that chemical transmission could be involved in the former.

claims.text: דייל ועמיתיו היו אחראים בעיקר להוכחת קיום העברה כימית מחוץ למערכת העצבים האוטונומית הפוסט-גנגליונית.
claims.quote: it was Dale and his associates who were mainly responsible for establishing the existence of chemical transmission outside the postganglionic autonomic nervous system

claims.text: בציטוט במאמר אחר מופיעה שנת 1920 לליל החלום.
claims.quote: The night before Easter Sunday of [1920] I awoke, turned on the light and jotted down a few notes on a tiny slip of thin paper.

claims.text: לפי גרסה נוספת, ליל החלום היה בפסחא 1920.
claims.quote: During the night before Easter Sunday, 1920, Loewi awoke with the idea for an experiment clearly in his mind.

claims.text: לפי האוניברסיטה הרפואית של גראץ, לוי מונה ב-1909 לקתדרה לפרמקולוגיה באוניברסיטת גראץ, ולימד שם עד 1938.
claims.quote: In 1909 he was appointed to the Chair of Pharmacology at the University of Graz, where he taught until 1938.

claims.text: החומר: Vagusstoff, אצטילכולין
claims.quote: He identified a substance, which he called Vagusstoff (later recognized as acetylcholine)

claims.text: בבוקר לא הצליח לפענח את כתב ידו.
claims.quote: but I was unable to decipher the scrawl.

claims.text: את החומר כינו Vagusstoff.
claims.quote: Loewi called this substance Vagusstoff since it was released from the vagus nerve.

claims.text: Vagusstoff היה האישור הראשון להעברה סינפטית כימית והמוליך העצבי הראשון שהתגלה.
claims.quote: Later, chemical analysis revealed the substance as acetylcholine, the first neurotransmitter to be identified.

claims.text: בוואגוס של הצפרדע שבה השתמש לוי יש סיבים מעכבים וסיבים מעוררים, ובחורף הסיבים המעכבים הם הרוב, ולכן לוי היה בר מזל שביצע את הניסויים בפברואר או במרץ.
claims.quote: In the winter the inhibitory fibers predominate

claims.text: בוואגוס של הצפרדע שבה השתמש לוי יש סיבים מעכבים וסיבים מעוררים, ובחורף הסיבים המעכבים הם הרוב, ולכן לוי היה בר מזל שביצע את הניסויים בפברואר או במרץ.
claims.quote: It is important that Loewi did the experiments in February and March
